title: Shared native worktree cache
objective: Make fresh parallel worktrees reuse content-addressed immutable native dependency and addon builds safely, so required validation does not rebuild GMP, FLINT, OpenBLAS, and graph or fail because an addon is absent.

handoff.summary: Added a verified content-addressed cache for FLINT and graph dependency prefixes and ABI-specific addons, shared through the Git common directory and restored automatically by parallel:new. Native validation now provisions through the cache and builds the root distribution before testing; changed-file checks use the same path. Publication revalidates source inputs before and after the build, validates temporary entries before atomic publication, and cannot publish a stale key. Restore is symlink-safe and transactional across all output roots. Locks are atomically initialized, heartbeat-aware, and never steal from a positively live local owner. Cache corruption, source races, path injection, rollback, lock recovery, toolchain invalidation, local-copy isolation, and real process concurrency have focused coverage. A real Linux x64 cold build took 6m45s, while a complete warm restore took 1.5s; one retained production identity occupies 212 MiB.
risks: Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 behavior is designed into keying, path handling, pnpm invocation, and atomic replacement, but the corresponding CI runners remain the final platform oracle.
The cache has no pruning policy yet, so distinct valid toolchain and source identities accumulate until removed manually.
Filesystems without copy-on-write clone support receive independent physical copies, trading extra disk space for the same isolation and correctness.

Restored FLINT and graph artifacts work through the repository's explicit include and library paths, but generated kernel_core.c provenance plus pkg-config .pc and libtool .la metadata retain the producer-worktree path. Normalize or rewrite those files before promising the cache to arbitrary downstream pkg-config, libtool, or debug-source consumers.
next_steps: Merge the integration lane and let each required platform seed its own native cache on the first cold validation.
Add cache status and pruning commands if normal development produces enough historical identities to make growth material.
Make generated FFI provenance and dependency metadata relocatable before exposing cached prefixes as a general downstream SDK.
